candidates.change_summary: Replace `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number;` so the lock-in block is immediate instead of the next block.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number - 1;` so the locked block is always in the past, immediately allowing settlement.
Delete `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` so lockInGuess can be called without sending 1 ether, changing the contract's balance and behavior for subsequent calls.
Delete `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` so the guess is never stored, causing settlement to never pay out.
Delete `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` so the block number remains 0, preventing settlement from ever proceeding.
Replace `require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0);` with `require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0);` so a user can only call lockInGuess if they already have a pending guess.
Delete the second require in lockInGuess so callers no longer need to send exactly 1 ether.
Delete the first require in lockInGuess so a caller may call it again even after already locking in a guess.
Replace the guess assignment in lockInGuess with a self-assignment so the stored guess hash is left unchanged.
Replace the block assignment in lockInGuess with a no-op self-assignment so the lock block number is never set.
Replace the first lockInGuess guard with a check that the caller has no existing nonzero block field, making the guard weaker so a caller can lock in repeatedly.
Change the ETH payment requirement from exactly 1 ether to at least 1 ether, so calls with more than 1 ether no longer revert.
Change the stored guess field assignment to use the current block number instead of the supplied hash, altering the stored guess value.
Change the lock-in block target from the next block to the current block, so the target block can already be mined.
Delete the line that resets block to 0, so settle can be called repeatedly with the same valid guess.
Replace `guesses[msg.sender].block` with `guesses[msg.sender].block + 1` in the require condition, allowing settlement one block earlier.
Delete the `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;` statement, so the guess remains active after settlement (and can be reused, unlike original).
Change the payout from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering the transferred amount on a correct guess.
Remove the payout entirely, so a correct guess transfers nothing (behavior changes from 2 ether to 0).
Swap the order: reset block to 0 after the transfer, so the transfer happens before state update (observable via reentrancy or gas griefing).
Change `guesses[msg.sender].guess` to a hardcoded value in the equality check, so settlement always fails (or succeeds for a random guess).
Change `blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block)` to `blockhash(block.number)`, altering the answer source and likely causing all guesses to fail or behave unpredictably.
Change `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0` to `guesses[msg.sender].block = 1`, so settlement leaves block non-zero and the guess remains active.
Remove `guesses[msg.sender].block != 0` requirement, allowing settle to be called without a prior valid lockInGuess.
Change `block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block` to `block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block`, allowing immediate settlement in the same block.

Replace `blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block)` with `keccak256(abi.encodePacked(blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block)))` (double hash), changing the answer and making correct guesses impossible under normal conditions.
Delete the entire line `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` inside lockInGuess (Note: that line is in lockInGuess, not settle. This edit is invalid per the requirement to edit only U001. I remove it.)
Change the settle guard from block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block, allowing settlement in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Change the unused-answer hash source from blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) to blockhash(block.number), so the answer depends on the current block instead of the locked block.
Delete the require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0) guard, allowing settle to be called when no guess is locked.
Move the guesses[msg.sender].block = 0 state update from before the transfer to after the transfer, changing reentrancy-visible behavior.
Change the settling branch condition from equality to inequality, paying out when the guess is wrong instead of when it matches.
Weaken the first settle guard so it only checks the stored guess, not the block field, allowing settlement of a zero-block guess and causing a different revert/success path.
Change the block-number guard from strictly greater than to greater-than-or-equal, so settlement can succeed one block too early.
Clear the stored guess instead of the stored block before the payout check, changing post-settlement state and reentrancy-visible behavior.
Always send the 2 ether payout regardless of whether the guess matches the computed answer.
Move the state-clearing write from before the external payout call to after it, exposing reentrant settlement before the block field is zeroed.
